title: Sales By Representative screen, filter and column look as designed
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "sbr-04-a4-sbr-c.png" (board 4.4), "sbr-05-a4-sbr-expanded.png" (board 4.5), "sbr-06-a4-filter-open.png" (board 4.6), "sbr-07-a4-sbr-labor-only.png" (board 4.7), "sbr-08-a4-columns-off.png" (board 4.8), "sbr-09-a4-columns-on.png" (board 4.9) and "sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png" (board 4.10) attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Today has one invoiced split work order (Labor {Sales-rep-A}, Parts {Sales-rep-B}), one invoiced work order with {Sales-rep-A} on both sides and one invoiced part sale with no shop supplies.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open in that browser window.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Compare the default report with the picture of board 4.4.
  2. Expand both representatives and compare with the picture of board 4.5.
  3. Open the Sales Type filter and compare with the picture of board 4.6.
  4. Select only Labor and compare with the picture of board 4.7, then select all three again.
  5. Open the column selector and compare with the pictures of boards 4.8 and 4.9 as you turn Sales Type on.
  6. Expand both representatives and compare with the picture of board 4.10.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: one row per representative; the filter reads "Sales Type: All"; no Sales Type column by default.
  • Step 2: the split invoice shows under both representatives; a side a representative did not sell shows a dash (including Shop Supplies on the Parts row); the part sale with no shop supplies shows a dash under Shop Supplies.
  • Step 3: the filter lists "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales", all ticked.
  • Step 4: only the labor side of each work order shows, as in the picture.
  • Step 5: "Sales Type" is the first entry, off by default; switching it on adds the column right after Status (and before Location when the Location column shows).
  • Step 6: the Sales Type column reads "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales" and "Labor, Parts"; columns line up as in the picture and nothing overlaps.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 10 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative), story SV-11272 (Story 8, Filter both sales reports by Sales Type)

  • S5-R10: “When one person, or Unassigned, holds both the Labor and the Parts side of a work order and the Sales Type filter includes both, the two show as one row whose Sales Type reads "Labor, Parts" and whose figures are the sum of both sides.”
  • S5-R15: “On a Labor row the parts columns show a dash, and on a Parts row the labor, hours and Shop Supplies columns show a dash, not $0.00. $0.00 is shown only for a real zero. A row that holds both sides, one person on both, keeps the report's rule that an invoice with no labor shows Labor Delta 0.0.”
  • S5-R15a: “On a Part Sales row, Shop Supplies shows the part sale's shop supplies, or a dash when the part sale has no shop supplies charge. $0.00 shows only when a shop supplies charge of $0.00 is on it.”
  • S5-R19: “An invoice row carries a "Sales Type" column, after Status and before Location (Status, Sales Type, Location), reading "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales" or "Labor, Parts".”
  • S5-R20: “The Sales Type column is offered in the report's column selector, first in its list.”
  • S5-R21: “The Sales Type column is off by default on screen, for every user.”
  • S8-R1: “Sales By Representative has a "Sales Type" filter with three options, in this order: "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales". All three are selected by default.”
  • S8-R3: “With all three selected the filter reads "Sales Type: All". With none it reads "Sales Type: None". Otherwise it reads the selected names in option order, for example "Sales Type: Labor, Parts".”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (19 Oct 2026), read 20 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 24: “24. (a) as the feature spec: a dash on screen and in the PDF, an empty cell in the CSV. The 0.0 rule still applies to an invoice with one person on both sides.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 25: “25. (a) A dash when the part sale has no shop supplies; $0.00 only when it has a shop supplies line that totals $0.00. The design's $0.00 is a sample-data mistake.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 26: “26. (a) Status, Sales Type, Location.”
  • Chris Ward's answer 36: “36. (b) Acceptable as shown, same as today's report.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, boards 4.4 One row per rep; 4.5 Expanded: Sales Type column off; 4.6 The Sales Type filter; 4.7 Labor only; 4.8 The column picker; 4.9 Sales Type switched on; 4.10 Expanded with Sales Type (the attached pictures are these boards).

Where the design and the PRD differ: The pictures show $0.00 under Shop Supplies on the Parts row (boards 4.5 and 4.10) and on the part sales, while the board 4.5 note (quoted below) says a side a rep did not sell shows a dash. Chris Ward ruled on 19 Oct 2026 for the PRD's dash, and said the design's $0.00 on the part sales is a sample-data mistake (answers 24 and 25, quoted above); this case follows them. The "Column Selection" tooltip covering the Sales Type switch (board 4.8) is acceptable as today (answer 36).

Design pictures attached to this case: sbr-04-a4-sbr-c.png, sbr-05-a4-sbr-expanded.png, sbr-06-a4-filter-open.png, sbr-07-a4-sbr-labor-only.png, sbr-08-a4-columns-off.png, sbr-09-a4-columns-on.png, sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png.
